driving_question: q0097 — the lock's life-cycle (DEEP continuation, Doctorow b0274)
book: Information Doesn't Want to Be Free (Cory Doctorow, 2014)
best_collision: The copy IS the marketing engine: the more copied Randall's comics get, the more he earns (c01937, p.84) — yet the lock, the only tool for controlling copies, is aimed at that very copy; and the RIAA's piracy math (c01941, p.84) prices the download as a lost album the buyer never wanted. The enforcer's tool targets the asset the artist profits from
quote: The more famous—the more copied—Randall's comics get, the more money he makes. He doesn't need to control or reduce copies. Good thing, because he knows he can't. (p.84)
mutation_note: cost disease did not cheapen the performing, but it handed the performer back his destiny — the capital (cameras, tickets, suites) fell to zero and the only fixed cost left is the time you can supply yourself; so the lock, aimed at the copy, is aimed at the very thing the abundance economy runs on, and the pirate-stat is the enforcer counting receipts for a customer who never existed
